### Check multi collinearity (VIF)
car library not working, make own vif function:
```{r}
# Calculate VIF for each numerical predictor
calculate_vif <- function(model) {
  
  # Get the model matrix
  X <- model.matrix(model)[, -1]
  
  # Calculate VIF for each column
  vif_values <- numeric(ncol(X))
  names(vif_values) <- colnames(X)
  
  for (i in seq_along(vif_values)) {
    
    other_vars <- X[, -i, drop = FALSE]
    target <- X[, i]
    
    auxiliary_model <- lm(target ~ other_vars)
    
    R2 <- summary(auxiliary_model)$r.squared
    
    vif_values[i] <- 1 / (1 - R2)
  }
  
  return(vif_values)
}
```

```{r}
vif_values <- calculate_vif(preliminary_model)
round(vif_values, 2)
```

Rough interpretation of VIF
VIF 1-2, little concern
VIF 2-5, moderate
VIF 5-10, high
VIF >10 Very high

Can remove cast_latitude, cast_longitude as they are highly correlated with haul_latitude, haul_longitude.

Can remove depth_cast as similar to depth_haul 

Even though fround before that trawl speed, time and length are their own variables, the VIF finds speed and time redundant relative to the other trawl variables. Therefore we will remove trawl_speed and trawl_time

Remove quadrant too as it was created from the latitude and longitude variables. This variable may be useful for more simpler models, but not for this multilinear regression model.

```{r}
model_2 <- lm(
  log_catch ~
    year +

    haul_longitude +

    bottom_temp +
    air_temp +
    barometer +
    trawl_length +

)

summary(model_2)
```
Model 2 explains 18.36% of variation, but model 1 explains 20.9%.


### Check collinearity
```{r}
vif_values_2 <- calculate_vif(model_2)

round(vif_values_2, 2)
```
Largest VIF is 4.02, which is generally acceptable. 

We can now use model 2 as a baseline model.

```{r}
summary(model_2)$coefficients
```

Similarly, depth_haul also has a high p-value of p=0.964. However this may suggest that the variable is non-linearly correlated with catch.

## TESTING STATION CATCH
1. Extract 2002-2022, divide into 10 years training/testing, repeat this process 100 times. 
2. Fit the regression model.
3. Predict station-level catch. Predict log_catch for each station in the held-out years, then transform predictions back to kilograms.
4. Compare predictions with observations. Calculate MAE, RMSE and MAPE across the testing stations, and summarise performance across the 100 repetitions.

```{r}
# --------------------------------------------------
# 1. Settings
# --------------------------------------------------

n_iterations <- 100
n_train_years <- 10
n_test_years <- 10

years <- 2002:2022

categorical_vars <- c(
  "ship_number", "weather", "cloud",
  "sea_state", "quadrant"
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 2. Prepare data
# --------------------------------------------------

df <- df %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    tow_station = as.character(tow_station),
    catch = as.numeric(catch),
    log_catch = ifelse(catch > 0, log(catch), NA_real_)
  )

# Convert categorical predictors to factors
for (v in categorical_vars) {
  if (v %in% names(df)) {
    df[[v]] <- as.factor(df[[v]])
  }
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 3. Define regression models
# --------------------------------------------------

preliminary_formula <- log_catch ~
  year +
  cast_latitude + cast_longitude +
  haul_latitude + haul_longitude +
  depth_cast + depth_haul +
  ship_number +
  wind_speed + wind_direction +
  weather + cloud + sea_state +
  bottom_temp + air_temp + barometer +
  trawl_speed + trawl_length +
  trawl_bearing + trawl_time +
  quadrant

simplified_formula <- log_catch ~
  year +
  haul_latitude + haul_longitude +
  depth_haul +
  ship_number +
  bottom_temp + air_temp + barometer +
  trawl_length + trawl_bearing

model_formulas <- list(
  "Preliminary" = preliminary_formula,
  "Simplified" = simplified_formula
)

# --------------------------------------------------
# 4. Function to fit a model and predict catches
#    with 95% prediction intervals
# --------------------------------------------------

fit_and_predict <- function(formula, train_data, test_data) {

  # Remove unused factor levels from training data
  train_data <- droplevels(train_data)

  # Match test factor levels to the training data.
  # Unseen levels become NA and will not be evaluated.
  for (v in categorical_vars) {
    if (v %in% all.vars(formula)) {
      if (v %in% names(train_data) &&
          is.factor(train_data[[v]])) {

        test_data[[v]] <- factor(
          test_data[[v]],
          levels = levels(train_data[[v]])
        )
      }
    }
  }

  # Fit the regression model
  fit <- lm(
    formula,
    data = train_data,
    na.action = na.exclude
  )

  # Duan smearing correction for log-transformed catch
  smearing_factor <- mean(
    exp(residuals(fit)),
    na.rm = TRUE
  )

  # Predict on the log-catch scale, including
  # 95% prediction intervals
  pred <- predict(
    fit,
    newdata = test_data,
    interval = "prediction",
    level = 0.95
  )

  # Transform predictions and interval bounds
  # back to the original catch scale
  data.frame(
    actual = test_data$catch,
    predicted = exp(pred[, "fit"]) * smearing_factor,
    lower = exp(pred[, "lwr"]) * smearing_factor,
    upper = exp(pred[, "upr"]) * smearing_factor
  )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 5. Function to calculate performance metrics
# --------------------------------------------------

calculate_metrics <- function(predictions) {

  actual <- predictions$actual
  predicted <- predictions$predicted
  lower <- predictions$lower
  upper <- predictions$upper

  # Observations with valid point predictions
  valid <- is.finite(actual) &
    is.finite(predicted) &
    is.finite(lower) &
    is.finite(upper)

  actual <- actual[valid]
  predicted <- predicted[valid]
  lower <- lower[valid]
  upper <- upper[valid]

  if (length(actual) == 0) {
    return(data.frame(
      n_evaluated = 0,
      MAE = NA_real_,
      RMSE = NA_real_,
      MAPE = NA_real_,
      Mean_Bias = NA_real_,
      R_squared = NA_real_,
      Coverage = NA_real_,
      Mean_Interval_Width = NA_real_
    ))
  }

  errors <- predicted - actual

  # MAPE is calculated only where actual catch > 0
  positive_actual <- actual > 0

  MAPE <- if (any(positive_actual)) {
    mean(
      abs(errors[positive_actual] /
            actual[positive_actual])
    ) * 100
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }

  # R-squared on the original catch scale
  R_squared <- if (
    length(actual) > 1 &&
    sum((actual - mean(actual))^2) > 0
  ) {
    1 - sum(errors^2) /
      sum((actual - mean(actual))^2)
  } else {
    NA_real_
  }

  # Percentage of actual catches within the
  # 95% prediction intervals
  coverage <- mean(
    actual >= lower & actual <= upper
  ) * 100

  # Average width of the prediction intervals
  interval_width <- mean(upper - lower)

  data.frame(
    n_evaluated = length(actual),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors)),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2)),
    MAPE = MAPE,
    Mean_Bias = mean(errors),
    R_squared = R_squared,
    Coverage = coverage,
    Mean_Interval_Width = interval_width
  )
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 6. Run repeated train-test validation
# --------------------------------------------------

regression_results <- list()

for (i in seq_len(n_iterations)) {

  # Randomly select 10 training years and 10
  # testing years; one year remains unused
  train_years <- sample(years, n_train_years)
  test_years <- sample(
    setdiff(years, train_years),
    n_test_years
  )

  train_data <- df %>%
    filter(year %in% train_years)

  test_data <- df %>%
    filter(year %in% test_years)

  # Store predictions from both models
  iteration_predictions <- list()

  for (model_name in names(model_formulas)) {

    iteration_predictions[[model_name]] <-
      tryCatch(
        fit_and_predict(
          formula = model_formulas[[model_name]],
          train_data = train_data,
          test_data = test_data
        ),
        error = function(e) NULL
      )
  }

  # Ensure both models are compared on exactly
  # the same test observations
  if (
    is.null(iteration_predictions[["Preliminary"]]) ||
    is.null(iteration_predictions[["Simplified"]])
  ) {
    next
  }

  preliminary_predictions <-
    iteration_predictions[["Preliminary"]]

  simplified_predictions <-
    iteration_predictions[["Simplified"]]

  common_valid <- with(
    preliminary_predictions,
    is.finite(actual) &
      is.finite(predicted) &
      is.finite(lower) &
      is.finite(upper)
  ) & with(
    simplified_predictions,
    is.finite(actual) &
      is.finite(predicted) &
      is.finite(lower) &
      is.finite(upper)
  )

  # Apply the same observations to both models
  preliminary_predictions <-
    preliminary_predictions[common_valid, ]

  simplified_predictions <-
    simplified_predictions[common_valid, ]

  for (model_name in names(model_formulas)) {

    predictions <- iteration_predictions[[model_name]]

    if (model_name == "Preliminary") {
      predictions <- preliminary_predictions
    } else {
      predictions <- simplified_predictions
    }

    metrics <- calculate_metrics(predictions)

    metrics$model <- model_name
    metrics$iteration <- i

    regression_results[[length(regression_results) + 1]] <-
      metrics
  }
}

# --------------------------------------------------
# 7. Combine results and summarise performance
# --------------------------------------------------

regression_results_df <- bind_rows(regression_results)

regression_summary <- regression_results_df %>%
  group_by(model) %>%
  summarise(
    Successful_Iterations = n(),

    Mean_Observations = mean(
      n_evaluated, na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Mean_MAE = mean(MAE, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_MAE = sd(MAE, na.rm = TRUE),

    Mean_RMSE = mean(RMSE, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_RMSE = sd(RMSE, na.rm = TRUE),

    Mean_MAPE = mean(MAPE, na.rm = TRUE),
    SD_MAPE = sd(MAPE, na.rm = TRUE),

    Mean_Bias = mean(Mean_Bias, na.rm = TRUE),

    Mean_R_squared = mean(
      R_squared, na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Mean_Coverage = mean(
      Coverage, na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    SD_Coverage = sd(
      Coverage, na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    Mean_Interval_Width = mean(
      Mean_Interval_Width, na.rm = TRUE
    ),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(regression_summary)

```



## TESTING TOTAL CATCH
Test model 2 and model 1
1. Extract 2002-2022, divide into 10 years training/testing
2. Fit regression model
3. Predict catch for testing years
4. Generate 1000 surveys
5. Repeat 100 times

Set up both models
```{r}
df <- read_excel("spring_historical_english.xlsx")

# Create log catch
df <- df |>
  mutate(
    catch = as.numeric(catch),
    log_catch = log(catch)
  )

# Formulas from your two fitted models
model_formulas <- list(
  "Preliminary Model" = formula(preliminary_model),
  "Model 2" = formula(model_2)
)

# All predictors required by both models
required_variables <- unique(
  unlist(lapply(model_formulas, all.vars))
)

# Keep rows with valid response and predictor values
df_test <- df |>
  filter(
    catch > 0,
    is.finite(catch),
    is.finite(log_catch),
    if_all(all_of(required_variables), ~ !is.na(.x))
  )

# Restrict testing to the chosen historical period
years <- sort(unique(
  df_test$year[
    df_test$year >= 2002 &
    df_test$year <= 2022
  ]
))

years <- tail(years, 20)

if (length(years) != 20) {
  stop("There must be 20 usable years in the selected period.")
}

df_test <- df_test |>
  filter(year %in% years)
```

```{r}

# Combine results from both models
results <- bind_rows(results_list)

head(results)

```


Compare models
```{r}
model_comparison <- results |>
  group_by(model) |>
  summarise(
    iterations = n(),

    coverage_percent = mean(covered) * 100,

    mean_absolute_error = mean(absolute_error, na.rm = TRUE),

    median_absolute_error = median(absolute_error, na.rm = TRUE),

    mean_interval_width = mean(interval_width, na.rm = TRUE),

    .groups = "drop"
  )

print(model_comparison)
```


Plot models
```{r}
ggplot(results, aes(x = iteration)) +

  geom_linerange(
    aes(ymin = lower_95, ymax = upper_95),
    colour = "steelblue",
    linewidth = 0.5
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(y = predicted_mean),
    colour = "steelblue",
    size = 1.3
  ) +

  geom_point(
    aes(y = actual_mean),
    colour = "red",
    size = 1.3
  ) +

  facet_wrap(
    ~ model,
    ncol = 1,
    labeller = as_labeller(c(
      "Preliminary Model" = "Preliminary Model",
      "Model 2" = "Simplified Model"
    ))
  ) +

  labs(
    title = "Regression Models: Simulated Mean Catch and 95% Intervals",
    subtitle = "Blue = simulated mean; red = observed mean",
    x = "Testing iteration",
    y = "Mean annual total catch (kg)"
  ) +

  theme_minimal() +

  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5)
  )
```
